original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-faithfully-flat-universally-injective}
Any faithfully flat ring map is universally injective.

final_content.statement: Let $R\to S$ be a faithfully flat homomorphism of commutative rings. For every $R$-module $T$ the canonical map $T\to T\otimes_RS$, $t\mapsto t\otimes1$, is injective. In other words, every faithfully flat ring map is universally injective as a morphism of $R$-modules.

semantic_review_note: Original L932–935 says any FAITHFULLY FLAT R→S is UNIVERSALLY INJECTIVE, defined in this section by injectivity T→T⊗_R S for EVERY R-module T. The expansion uses universal injection of modules, not the different notion of radicial scheme morphisms.

final_content.statement:
For a commutative ring $R$, define the contravariant $R$-module functor $C(M)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb Z}(M,\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z)$, with $R$-action $(r\cdot\lambda)(m)=\lambda(rm)$. Then $C$ is an exact contravariant functor: for each short exact sequence $0\to M'\to M\to M''\to0$ the sequence
$$0\to C(M'')\to C(M)\to C(M')\to0$$
is exact. Furthermore, it reflects monomorphisms and epimorphisms: an $R$-linear map $u:M\to N$ is injective if and only if $C(u):C(N)\to C(M)$ is surjective, and $u$ is surjective if and only if $C(u)$ is injective.
hypotheses: $R$ is a commutative ring and $C(M)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb Z}(M,\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z)$.
conclusions: The contravariant character-dual functor is exact and detects injections/surjections by reversing them.

semantic_review_note: Original L947–964 defines CONTRAVARIANT C(M)=Hom_Ab(M,Q/Z) with R-action (rλ)(m)=λ(rm), then asserts C is EXACT and REFLECTS injections and surjections. The reconstruction correctly reverses arrow directions: injective u iff surjective C(u) and vice versa.

hypotheses: $u:M\to N$ is a map of $R$-modules, with $C$ the character dual functor.
conclusions: Universal injectivity of $u$ is equivalent to $C(u)$ being split surjective.

semantic_review_note: Original L1001–1005 characterizes UNIVERSAL INJECTIVITY of arbitrary module map f:M→N by SPLIT SURJECTIVITY of C(f):C(N)→C(M). The proposed equivalence demands an R-LINEAR section, not just surjectivity of C(f).

hypotheses: $f:R\to S$ is a commutative-ring homomorphism, with the usual category of module descent data.
conclusions: Fully faithful descent, effective descent, and universal injectivity are equivalent.

semantic_review_note: Original L1289–1297 gives THREE EQUIVALENT conditions for ring f:R→S: descent morphism for modules, EFFECTIVE descent morphism and UNIVERSALLY INJECTIVE ring map. The text restores f from section setup, defines comparison functor, and preserves all three directions.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-flat-to-injective}
If $M \in \text{Mod}_R$ is flat, then $C(M)$ is an injective $R$-module.

final_content.statement: For a commutative ring $R$, define the contravariant $R$-module functor $C(M)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb Z}(M,\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z)$, with $R$-action $(r\cdot\lambda)(m)=\lambda(rm)$. If $M$ is a flat $R$-module, then $C(M)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb Z}(M,\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z)$ is an injective object of $\operatorname{Mod}_R$; equivalently, the contravariant functor $\operatorname{Hom}_R(-,C(M))$ is exact.
hypotheses: $R$ is commutative and $M$ is flat over $R$.
conclusions: The character dual $C(M)$ is an injective $R$-module.

semantic_review_note: Original L1332–1335 states if R-module M is FLAT then its CONTRAVARIANT dual C(M)=Hom_Z(M,Q/Z) is INJECTIVE as an R-module. The draft retains flatness on M and injectivity of C(M), not converses.

final_content.statement: A homomorphism $f:R\to S$ of commutative rings is universally injective (or pure as an $R$-module map) if, for every $R$-module $T$, the canonical map $T\to T\otimes_R S$ is injective. Let $M$ be an $R$-module. For each one of the following properties, $M$ has the property over $R$ if and only if $M\otimes_RS$ has it over $S$: (a) finitely generated; (b) finitely presented; (c) flat; (d) faithfully flat; (e) finite projective (finitely generated projective). The same pure ring map $f$ is used in each assertion.
hypotheses: $f:R\to S$ is universally injective/pure, and $M$ is an $R$-module.
conclusions: Finite generation, finite presentation, flatness, faithful flatness, and finite projectivity descend and ascend along $f$.

semantic_review_note: Original L1326–1329 fixes a UNIVERSALLY INJECTIVE ring map R→S throughout the subsection. The theorem L1356–1372 says EACH of finite generation, finite presentation, flat, faithfully flat and FINITE PROJECTIVE descends from M⊗_R S to M and ascends conversely. The proposal restores the standing purity premise for every independent equivalence.

final_content.statement: A homomorphism $f:R\to S$ of commutative rings is universally injective (or pure as an $R$-module map) if, for every $R$-module $T$, the canonical map $T\to T\otimes_R S$ is injective. Let $A$ be an $R$-algebra. Each of the following properties of the structure map $R\to A$ holds if and only if the corresponding property holds for $S\to A\otimes_RS$: (a) finite type; (b) finite presentation; (c) formally unramified; (d) unramified; (e) étale.
hypotheses: $R\to S$ is universally injective/pure, and $A$ is an $R$-algebra.
conclusions: Each listed finite-presentation/differential/étale property of $A$ is equivalent to its validity after extension of scalars to $S$.

semantic_review_note: Original L1445–1463 in the SAME subsection assumes universally injective R→S and lists five independent R-algebra properties of A: finite type, finite presentation, formally unramified, unramified and ÉTALE. Each is equivalent to base-changed property over S; all are retained.
